reduction.quote: Modeling: claiming game with "pick any piece" — proved (and verified by brute force) that optimal play = greedy, so LB gets odd-position pieces (sorted decreasing).
reduction.witness: MISSING STATEMENT: a proof that, for any multiset of piece lengths, optimal alternating play makes each player take the currently largest remaining piece, so that Liu obtains the pieces in odd positions of the decreasing sort and his total is (1+D)/2 with D = p_1 - p_2 + p_3 - ... . The quoted passage only asserts this ('proved') and appeals to brute-force verification on finite grids; no exchange/strategy-stealing argument, no induction on the number of pieces, and no general proof appears anywhere in the text. Brute force on grids of K atoms covers only finitely many configurations, not all multisets.
reduction.load_bearing: Every later statement (the matching formula for D, Part A's target D >= delta, Part B's target D <= T_n S) is phrased in terms of the alternating sum D, so without this reduction none of the bounds translate into guarantees about Liu's actual share.

lower_bound.quote: Part A (LB guarantee) proof sketched above via matching formula + component decomposition + block lemma — needs writing + numeric checks.
lower_bound.witness: MISSING STATEMENT: a complete written proof that for the family a_i = 2^{i-1}/(2^{n+1}-1), i=1..n+1, EVERY subdivision by at most n cuts yields D >= 1/(2^{n+1}-1). The text presents the argument only as a compressed sketch that it itself flags as unwritten and unverified: the key matching identity 'sum p_{2k} = max_mu sum min(p,q)' is asserted 'by an exchange argument' with the argument omitted; the per-component inequality w_I <= cost(component) is compressed to a parenthetical '(algebra: ... then triangle ineq)'; the exclusion of odd-cycle components is justified by 'checked numerically by hand: triangle counterexample'; and the final specialization of the general super-increasing lemma to the geometric family with delta = 1/(2^{n+1}-1) is never carried out. A sketch whose lemmas are asserted rather than proved is not an all-cases argument.
lower_bound.load_bearing: The lower bound c_n >= 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) rests entirely on this Part A chain (matching formula -> slack counting -> tree component -> block lemma), and the text explicitly defers its writing and verification.

upper_bound.quote: BUT such a signed sum is NOT always realizable by cancel/chain ops (e.g. $\{1,2\}$: only $|2-1|$ realizable, not $2+1$). Realizability gap.
upper_bound.witness: MISSING STATEMENT: for EVERY Liu division into at most n+1 pieces, an explicit Xiang reply using at most n cuts forcing D <= S/(2^{n+1}-1). The text obtains only the pigeonhole existence of a nonzero sign vector delta in {-1,0,1}^{n+1} with |sum delta_i a_i| <= T_n S, and then states that such a signed sum need not be realizable by Xiang's cut operations, i.e. the construction converting the small signed sum into an actual cut strategy is absent. The remaining candidate ('min over subsets of greedy chain') is described as empirical and 'needs verification & proof'.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Without the realizability construction there is no Xiang strategy at all, so no upper bound on c_n is established; the text itself labels Part B 'still open'.

parsed.notes: Correct closed form given, but explicitly as a conjecture verified only for n=1,2,3 on grids. Reduction asserted via brute force. Part A is a self-declared sketch with key lemmas (exchange argument, per-component inequality, odd-cycle exclusion) asserted or checked by hand. Part B open due to acknowledged realizability gap.
